socialEngineering.label: MODULE 02 · SOCIAL ENGINEERING
socialEngineering.title: Reconstructing a digital trail
socialEngineering.description: See how everyday details can be combined into a manipulation pretext, then decide how to reduce that exposure.
socialEngineering.safeNote: SAFE SIMULATION · People, organizations, and artifacts are fictional

briefing.title: Choose attack vectors
briefing.description: A social engineer does not hack a system; they target people. Choose 2 to 5 kinds of information you might share online to see how an attacker could combine them into leverage.

board.title: Choose 2–5 synthetic artifacts
board.description: This board contains fictional examples only. It does not search real people, accounts, or sites.

artifacts.title: Everyday Photo & Work Desk
artifacts.value: A coffee photo or desk setup
artifacts.exposure: A screen may reveal internal apps; the background can expose CCTV placement or a physical ID badge.
artifacts.mitigation: Check the background before posting. Crop or blur screens, badges, and location clues; avoid live workplace posts.

artifacts.title: Fitness Tracker & Routine
artifacts.exposure: Repeated routes and schedules can map routines, when a home is empty, or when someone is away from their phone.
artifacts.mitigation: Make routes private and delay uploads until the activity is over. Remove routines and precise locations from public profiles.

artifacts.title: Public Social-Media Complaint
artifacts.exposure: A post may expose an unredacted tracking number, customer ID, or phone number.
artifacts.mitigation: Redact tracking numbers, customer IDs, and contact details. Discuss transaction details through a support channel you opened yourself.

artifacts.title: Celebrating a Career Move
artifacts.exposure: New-employee status can attract fake HR/IT messages before someone knows the rules or support team.
artifacts.mitigation: Review who can see job updates. Verify HR/IT instructions through a known internal directory or channel before acting.

artifacts.title: Family Ecosystem Exposure
artifacts.value: Stories about a child, school, or pickup
artifacts.exposure: A child's name, school, or regular pickup relative can make a pretext feel familiar.
artifacts.mitigation: Limit public names and family schedules. Agree on a safeword and confirm emergencies using a known phone number.

extraction.title: Extracting Digital Residue...
extraction.description: The findings below follow the artifacts and pairings you selected. No real data is searched for or sent.

pretext.title: Threat model · pretexting
pretext.description: The examples below are static, neutralized simulations. Notice how two clues can make a story feel more believable.
pretext.safeLabel: NEUTRALIZED SIMULATION EXAMPLES · do not follow any instructions

mitigation.title: Quarantine data · mitigation
mitigation.description: Apply OPSEC steps that directly close exposure paths created by your selected combination.
mitigation.choiceLabel: Choose one action you will apply

options.label: Minimize public details
options.description: Reduce locations, routines, and transaction details that can be combined.

options.label: Separate identity contexts
options.description: Avoid connecting personal, work, and family details in the same public trail.

options.label: Verify through an independent channel
options.description: Contact the organization through a known official channel, not details in an incoming message.

visual_routine.title: Desk photo + fitness routine
visual_routine.extraction: An app visible on a screen can be paired with the time its owner is away from the desk and phone.
visual_routine.pretext: Simulation: a message posing as IT support names an app visible in the photo and arrives when the exercise routine may distract its recipient.
visual_routine.mitigation: Make exercise routes private or delayed and inspect the sender domain. Contact support through an internal directory you open yourself.

visual_complaint.title: Desk photo + transaction complaint
visual_complaint.extraction: An unredacted tracking number can be combined with workplace, badge, or desk-location clues.
visual_complaint.pretext: Simulation: someone posing as a courier connects a parcel complaint to the workplace and asks for action through a work channel.
visual_complaint.mitigation: Redact tracking numbers and do not let workplace details become an alternate route for personal deliveries. Verify in the official courier app.

visual_career.title: Desk photo + new-job announcement
visual_career.extraction: New-employee status combines with app, operating-system, or workplace identity clues visible in a photo.
visual_career.pretext: Simulation: a fake IT-support account offers a work tool and references details visible in the photo.
visual_career.mitigation: Do not install or open files based on a message. Confirm in person or through a known internal IT channel.

visual_family.title: Desk photo + family post
visual_family.extraction: Workplace clues can be connected to a child's name or school location mentioned in a post.
visual_family.pretext: Simulation: a message posing as HR connects a workplace benefit to family information shared publicly.
visual_family.mitigation: Separate family and work trails. HR should not request family data through a link in an unexpected message.

routine_complaint.title: Fitness routine + transaction complaint
routine_complaint.extraction: Times when a phone is rarely checked can be paired with a delivery problem the owner is waiting to resolve.
routine_complaint.pretext: Simulation: an urgent delivery notice appears during exercise, using divided attention and a visible complaint as context.
routine_complaint.mitigation: Delay route posts and open the courier app independently. Do not use links or deadlines supplied in an incoming message.

routine_career.title: Fitness routine + new job
routine_career.extraction: Offline hours meet a new employee's pressure to appear responsive.
routine_career.pretext: Simulation: a message posing as a manager requests a file while the recipient is exercising and calls out their new status.
routine_career.mitigation: Disable public live tracking. Verify manager requests through a usual channel; time pressure is not proof of authority.

routine_family.title: Fitness routine + family information
routine_family.extraction: An offline pattern can be combined with a child's name and a fictional pickup relative.
routine_family.pretext: Simulation: a fake emergency call contacts a relative and claims the account owner is unreachable while exercising.
routine_family.mitigation: Agree on a family safeword and out-of-band verification. Schools and relatives should not act on financial requests from callers.

complaint_career.title: Transaction complaint + new job
complaint_career.extraction: A public tracking number meets new-employee status and the desire to appear professional.
complaint_career.pretext: Simulation: a supposed delivery service adds a request for workplace data under the pretext of priority service.
complaint_career.mitigation: A delivery service does not need employment data to resolve a parcel. Redact tracking details and verify in the official app.

complaint_family.title: Transaction complaint + family information
complaint_family.extraction: An open parcel issue can be linked to a child's name, school, or named pickup relative.
complaint_family.pretext: Simulation: a fake courier message mentions a relative or school to request a code or a handoff change.
complaint_family.mitigation: Never give an OTP or verification code to a courier or caller. Confirm delivery in the official app and contact family through a saved number.

career_family.title: New job + family information
career_family.extraction: A new-employee announcement can combine with child or school context to make a benefits story feel personal.
career_family.pretext: Simulation: a message posing as HR ties family-benefit registration to an urgent deadline.
career_family.mitigation: Zero Trust applies to internal messages too. Ask HR through a saved company channel; do not send family documents through message links.

executableFile.label: MODULE 03 · DOCUMENT ANALYSIS
executableFile.title: Risky Document Analysis
executableFile.description: This message offers an urgent delivery document. Inspect the source, filename, and extension before acting.
executableFile.safeNote: SAFE SIMULATION · No real file is available or executed

scenario.message: A delivery invoice needs review before 12:00. Download the document to update its status.

inspect.title: Open the file details one by one
inspect.description: The complete filename and the real extension decide what would run. Every detail here is fictional and cannot be downloaded.
inspect.note: An .exe extension is not automatically malicious, but an unexpected file from an untrusted source should be stopped and verified.
inspect.prompt: Open at least two details before you continue.
inspect.requirement: Open at least two file details.
inspect.clickInstruction: Click a detail label to reveal its check result. Open at least two details before continuing.

verify.label: Verify through an official channel
verify.description: Check the order or sender through a channel you already know.

ignore.label: Delete or ignore
ignore.description: Stop interacting with the message and file.

report.label: Report the message
report.description: Mark the message through a trusted reporting path.

analysis.label: FILE ANALYSIS · SIMULATION
analysis.unsafe: Opening or downloading an unexpected file advances a risky route. No real file is created, downloaded, or run.
analysis.safe: An official channel or ending interaction interrupts the file route before a device action occurs.
analysis.whyValue: A filename can hide its actual extension; the source and context still need inspection.
analysis.saferValue: Do not open an unexpected file. Verify the claim through a trusted channel, then report it if appropriate.

verify.title: Verify through an official channel
verify.description: A delivery claim can be checked without opening the file: look up the order in a channel you already trust, never through the link in the message.
verify.appNote: Simulation · the channel you opened yourself
verify.prompt: Look up the order in the official channel
verify.resultTitle: No such document in your account
verify.resultBody: The official channel has no invoice (.pdf.exe) and the sender is not the courier's domain. The claim did not come from the courier.
